proof:
Source: step 4 of the selected proof (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2)), the plane-ball measure H^n(P ∩ B̄_s(0)) = ω_n s^n, stated directly for a subspace P with finrank P = n. Provenance (orientation only): the same argument, for P = T.plane with T ∈ G(N, n), was accepted on another DAG branch for a lemma named intcpt_canon_plane_closedBall_hausdorff. That declaration is not available on this branch. Do not reference it; prove this child under its own name exactly as below. Stating the lemma for a Submodule removes the Grassmannian.ofSubmodule detour. The proof is self-contained.

Notation: P is viewed as a real inner product space with the restricted inner product and the subspace (Borel) σ-algebra; hP : finrank ℝ P = n; ι : P → ℝ^N is the inclusion (Subtype.val).

1. P ∩ closedBall 0 r = ι(closedBall (0 : P) r). Indeed, z lies in the left side iff z ∈ P and ‖z‖ ≤ r, iff z = ι(w) for some w ∈ P with ‖w‖ = ‖z‖ ≤ r. Prove it by ext, using ⟨z, hz⟩ for one inclusion and w.2 for the other.

2. ι is an isometry (isometry_subtype_coe). Isometries preserve the Euclidean Hausdorff measure of images (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), so μHE[n](ι(closedBall (0:P) r)) = μHE[n]_P(closedBall (0:P) r), where μHE[n]_P is μHE[n] on the metric space P.

3. On every finite-dimensional real inner product space E, μHE[finrank E] = volume (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Taking E = P and rewriting finrank ℝ P = n inside this equation gives μHE[n]_P = volume_P.

4. volume_P is an additive Haar measure on P. So for r ≥ 0, volume_P(closedBall (0:P) r) = ofReal(r^(finrank P)) · volume_P(ball (0:P) 1) = ofReal(r^n) · volume_P(ball (0:P) 1) (Measure.addHaar_closedBall, then hP). This also holds for n = 0 and for r = 0.

5. Let e : P ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) be the coordinate map of an orthonormal basis of P indexed by Fin n, e.g. ((stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ P).reindex (finCongr hP)).repr. A linear isometry equivalence between finite-dimensional inner product spaces preserves volume (LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving). Also e⁻¹(ball 0 1) = ball (0:P) 1, because ‖e w‖ = ‖w‖. Since balls are measurable (measurableSet_ball), MeasurePreserving.measure_preimage gives volume_P(ball (0:P) 1) = volume(ball (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1) = unitBallVolume n (the definition of unitBallVolume).

6. Combining steps 1–5 with ofReal(r^n) = ofReal(r)^n for r ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pow): μHE[n](P ∩ closedBall 0 r) = ofReal(r)^n · unitBallVolume n = unitBallVolume n · ofReal(r)^n (mul_comm). ∎ (For n = 0, P = {0} and both sides equal 1, consistent with the general argument.)

Lean route (checked in a scratch copy after import GMT.Ch08.Submission; axioms propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound): prove the set identity of step 1 by ext; obtain hvol : (μHE[n] : Measure P) = volume from InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume (V := P) by rwa [hP]; rw [himage, isometry_subtype_coe.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, hvol, Measure.addHaar_closedBall volume (0 : P) hr, hP]; prove volume (ball (0:P) 1) = unitBallVolume n with e.measurePreserving.measure_preimage measurableSet_ball.nullMeasurableSet after ext/simp for the preimage; finish with ENNReal.ofReal_pow hr and mul_comm.
key_steps: P ∩ B̄_r(0) is the image of the closed r-ball of the n-dimensional inner product space P under the isometric inclusion.
